newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banking union seeks 35-hour working week.
newsitem.headline: German banking union seeks 35-hour working week.

text.p: German banking and insurance union HBV said on Wednesday it would be seeking a cut in the working week to 35 hours from 39 hours when it meets employers in the sector for wage talks on Thursday.
It said such a move would help offset the effects of current job losses among banks, securing 50,000 out of the current 450,000 jobs in the industry.

Along with white-collar union DAG, its joint negotiator in the wage round, it said it would also be calling on the banks not to implement a 20 percent cut in sick pay entitlements made possible by a new federal law late last year.
Following large-scale protests, bank employers have held back from instituting the cuts until new clauses on the issue can be agreed and put into worker contracts.

Renewed debate on reduced work-hours has been prompted by a proposal last week by Klaus Zwickel, head of the giant metal and engineering trade union IG Metall, for a 32-hour general working week to help reduce unemployment.
Employer groups have reacted largely negatively to the suggestion, saying that this would only make labour in Germany yet more expensive and thus discourage job creation.

HBV said however that if employers were willing to come to agreements on work-hours it would in turn be ready to discuss new working arrangements related to Saturday opening, which German banks are keen to try out.
